direction: Every outage update says what happened, who is affected, what is not yet known, and when the next update comes, then keeps that time.
dont_over_correct: Do not promise a restoration time the crew has not given. Do not send an update every few minutes with nothing new; pick a cadence that fits the outage and say so (see the cadence sources in section 4). Do not blame the weather or a vendor to dodge ownership.
prompt: Every outage update gives a next-update clock time, and an update goes out by it.
design: Name the cause in plain words when it is known.
Give the next update time as a clock time.
Say what is unknown and why.
Update on or before the stated time.
Show estimates as given by the outage system, with the time they were made.
Offer a person and the safety route.
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: outage.cause, outage.area, outage.crew_status, outage.estimate, outage.next_update_at?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt, the agent's server code?

evals.behaviour: Cause named: Name the cause in plain words when it is known
evals.pass_if: Says a damaged transformer is the cause, in plain words.

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: no spam when nothing is new: Don't over-correct
evals.pass_if: No updates between the promised times.
evals.fail_if: A guessed estimate, or spam updates

guardrail.condition: an outage status reply has no next-update clock time
